# Homepage wall

_The homepage wall as it is published: every card's words beside the entry it expresses and the product features it draws on. The cards are authored in [`site/wall/deck.ts`](../../../../site/wall/deck.ts), which the homepage loads in the browser. This page is where to review them against the [Human Benefit Canon](../feature-canon-human-benefits.md), the [Agent Benefit Canon](../feature-canon-agent-benefits.md), the [`consequence-canon.md`](consequence-canon.md), and the [`claims-and-evidence.md`](claims-and-evidence.md) ledger. The [feature canon](../feature-canon.md) owns the features. [The wall's deck, cards, and glyphs](../../90-site/wall-deck-cards-and-glyphs.md) explains how the page shows a card._

68 cards · 52 benefit · 13 statement · 3 numeral · 7 lenses · 76 of 144 feature nodes drawn on.

## How to use this page

- Read a card against the entry it expresses. A card says in a visitor's words what that entry establishes, and the entry's own canon bounds how far the card may go.
- Check the features before changing one. A card draws on the feature nodes its words depend on, chosen from the nodes its entry rests on. Removing or reshaping a node means rewriting or removing each card listed beside it under [Features on the wall](#features-on-the-wall).
- Change a card in `site/wall/deck.ts`, then regenerate this page. The deck test refuses a card that draws on a missing node, or on a node its entry does not rest on.

### Take the project further

9 cards · lens: Run more at once.

#### Many agents, one machine

- **Card:** `parallel-work-on-one-machine` · benefit
- **Line:** Run agents in parallel, each in its own copy of your project.
- **Opened:** Every task gets its own folder and branch, plus its own ports and databases where you've declared them. If two tasks edit the same file, discern points out the overlap before the work comes together.
- **Link:** `/docs/guides/coordinate-parallel-tasks`
- **Expresses:** Human benefit · [Keep several tasks moving at the same time](../feature-canon-human-benefits.md#keep-several-tasks-moving-at-the-same-time)
- **Draws on:** Deterministic identity (`worktree-identity`) · Per-worktree resources (`worktree-resources`) · The fleet view (`fleet`)

#### Start the big change you keep putting off.

- **Card:** `statement-cheap-failure-buys-bold-work` · statement
- **Opened:** A failed attempt stays on its own branch, away from your main one. Throw it away, or run several approaches and keep the best.
- **Link:** `/docs/understand/worktrees-and-trunk`
- **Expresses:** Consequence · [When failing is cheap, you start the work you used to talk yourself out of](consequence-canon.md#when-failing-is-cheap-you-start-the-work-you-used-to-talk-yourself-out-of)
- **Draws on:** Isolated worktrees (`worktrees`)

#### Run three tasks as easily as one.

- **Card:** `statement-parallel-by-default` · statement
- **Opened:** Every task gets its own copy of the project, so starting a third takes no more setup than starting the first. The work still has to split along real seams.
- **Link:** `/docs/guides/coordinate-parallel-tasks`
- **Expresses:** Consequence · [Parallel stops being a special occasion](consequence-canon.md#parallel-stops-being-a-special-occasion)
- **Draws on:** Start (`start`) · Deterministic identity (`worktree-identity`) · Per-worktree resources (`worktree-resources`)

#### Hand off bigger goals

- **Card:** `shape-substantial-work` · benefit
- **Line:** Turn one big goal into complete briefs your agents can run with.
- **Opened:** Your agent finds the natural seams in the work and writes each brief to stand alone. Run the pieces side by side, or in stages when one depends on another.
- **Link:** `/docs/guides/delegate-work`
- **Expresses:** Human benefit · [Turn a large objective into work agents can carry](../feature-canon-human-benefits.md#turn-a-large-objective-into-work-agents-can-carry)
- **Draws on:** Delegate work (`skill-delegate-work`)

#### Don't run tests twice

- **Card:** `agent-resume-after-interruption` · benefit
- **Line:** If your agent loses a long test run, it reads the result back.
- **Opened:** A long run saves its progress and its final result as it goes. An agent that loses the connection reads them back instead of starting the run again.
- **Link:** `/docs/guides/recover-an-interrupted-task`
- **Expresses:** Agent benefit · [Resume after interruption](../feature-canon-agent-benefits.md#resume-after-interruption)
- **Draws on:** Progress and reconnect (`progress`)

#### Build on pending work

- **Card:** `compose-staged-work` · benefit
- **Line:** Start the next task on top of work you haven't merged yet.
- **Opened:** A follow-up can begin from an earlier task's tested commit while that one waits for your approval. Each task still merges only when you approve it.
- **Link:** `/docs/guides/coordinate-parallel-tasks#build-on-work-before-it-lands`
- **Expresses:** Human benefit · [Start the next task before the last one lands](../feature-canon-human-benefits.md#start-the-next-task-before-the-last-one-lands)
- **Draws on:** Composing unlanded work (`compose-below-trunk`) · Accept (`accept`)

#### Walk away mid-task

- **Card:** `resume-later` · benefit
- **Line:** Leave a task half done and resume it in a new session.
- **Opened:** The task's folder, branch, and setup stay where you left them. A new session asks discern where things stand and gets the next step.
- **Link:** `/docs/guides/recover-an-interrupted-task`
- **Expresses:** Human benefit · [Walk away mid-task and pick up where you left off](../feature-canon-human-benefits.md#walk-away-mid-task-and-pick-up-where-you-left-off)
- **Draws on:** Status (`status`)

#### Stop playing messenger

- **Card:** `wait-without-relay` · benefit
- **Line:** Agents wait for each other's work, then carry on without a nudge.
- **Opened:** A task can pause until another passes its tests or joins your main branch, then carry on by itself.
- **Link:** `/docs/guides/wait-for-another-task`
- **Expresses:** Human benefit · [Stop playing messenger between your agents](../feature-canon-human-benefits.md#stop-playing-messenger-between-your-agents)
- **Draws on:** Awaiting a fleet condition (`await`) · Await the fleet (`skill-await-the-fleet`)

#### Merge in any order

- **Card:** `land-finished-work-as-the-project-moves` · benefit
- **Line:** Finished work still merges after other changes land, retested on the combined code.
- **Opened:** A temporary copy combines both changes, your tests run on the result, and only what passed merges. A real conflict goes back to the agent that wrote the change.
- **Link:** `/docs/guides/finish-and-land-a-change#when-other-work-lands-first`
- **Expresses:** Human benefit · [Keep finished work moving as the project moves](../feature-canon-human-benefits.md#keep-finished-work-moving-as-the-project-moves)
- **Draws on:** Integration worktrees (`integration-landings`) · Accept (`accept`)

### Spend more time on the product

9 cards · lens: Review less.

#### Review what matters

- **Card:** `reduce-routine-review` · benefit
- **Line:** Stop checking whether the tests ran, and review what the change does.
- **Opened:** Each finished change arrives with a record of which of your project's commands passed. Your attention can go to behavior, design, and risk.
- **Link:** `/docs/guides/finish-and-land-a-change`
- **Expresses:** Human benefit · [Review less, knowing what already passed](../feature-canon-human-benefits.md#review-less-knowing-what-already-passed)
- **Draws on:** The quality gate (`gate`) · Proof (`proof`)

#### No wasted checks

- **Card:** `run-relevant-checks` · benefit
- **Line:** Checks for one part of your project run only when that part changes.
- **Opened:** You name an area, such as your docs, and the check it needs, such as a link checker. Your tests and other everyday commands still run on every change.
- **Link:** `/docs/guides/finish-and-land-a-change`
- **Expresses:** Human benefit · [Run the checks relevant to this change](../feature-canon-human-benefits.md#run-the-checks-relevant-to-this-change)
- **Draws on:** Scopes (`scope-gates`)

#### More work comes back than you have to read.

- **Card:** `statement-review-grows-slower-than-output` · statement
- **Opened:** Routine checking happens before a change reaches you, and you can give routine approvals in advance. How deeply you review still depends on the change.
- **Link:** `/docs/guides/finish-and-land-a-change`
- **Expresses:** Consequence · [More work comes back than you have to read](consequence-canon.md#more-work-comes-back-than-you-have-to-read)
- **Draws on:** The quality gate (`gate`) · Proof (`proof`) · Landing authority is proved per invocation (`consent-attestations`)

#### See what needs you

- **Card:** `decisions-in-one-view` · benefit
- **Line:** One screen shows every task and which ones are waiting on you.
- **Opened:** Run discern in your project folder to open the desk, a view of your tasks sorted by what each needs from you. There's no need to visit every session to ask how it's going.
- **Link:** `/docs/guides/coordinate-parallel-tasks`
- **Expresses:** Human benefit · [See which tasks need a decision](../feature-canon-human-benefits.md#see-which-tasks-need-a-decision)
- **Draws on:** The desk (`desk`) · Owner-attention channel (`owner-attention`)

#### Catch the forgotten file

- **Card:** `catch-related-files` · benefit
- **Line:** Know when a change skips a file that usually goes with it.
- **Opened:** Your project's history shows which files tend to change together, such as a module and its test. The nudge is a hint drawn from habit, so you and your agent judge whether it applies.
- **Link:** `/docs/guides/improve-the-practice`
- **Expresses:** Human benefit · [Catch related files before the change closes](../feature-canon-human-benefits.md#catch-related-files-before-the-change-closes)
- **Draws on:** Coupling (`coupling`)

#### Less checking, more deciding.

- **Card:** `statement-the-job-moves-up-a-level` · statement
- **Opened:** Agents carry the coordination, the testing, and the record of what passed. Your time goes to briefs, design, and deciding what merges.
- **Link:** `/docs/guides/delegate-work`
- **Expresses:** Consequence · [Your job moves up a level](consequence-canon.md#your-job-moves-up-a-level)
- **Draws on:** Delegate work (`skill-delegate-work`) · Checkpoints (`checkpoints`) · Agent instructions (`instructions`)

#### Standing review questions

- **Card:** `judgment-at-the-change` · benefit
- **Line:** Write a review question once, and agents answer it on every matching change.
- **Opened:** You choose the files that trigger each question, such as whether a database change can be undone. This is what discern calls a checkpoint, and an unmet answer waits for you.
- **Link:** `/docs/understand/checkpoints`
- **Expresses:** Human benefit · [Ask the judgment questions when the change happens](../feature-canon-human-benefits.md#ask-the-judgment-questions-when-the-change-happens)
- **Draws on:** Checkpoints (`checkpoints`)

#### Less noise for agents

- **Card:** `context-for-the-task` · benefit
- **Line:** Results stay short, so your agent's attention goes to your code.
- **Opened:** Each result is short and names the next step. Long output keeps its start and end, and the full text goes to a file.
- **Link:** `/docs/start/how-discern-works`
- **Expresses:** Human benefit · [Use agent context on the task itself](../feature-canon-human-benefits.md#use-agent-context-on-the-task-itself)
- **Draws on:** Context is a budget (`context-budget`) · Authored Markdown results (`authored-markdown-results`)

#### Failures you can use

- **Card:** `useful-failures-sooner` · benefit
- **Line:** Every failure comes with its output and the command to reproduce it.
- **Opened:** A run stops early once a failure makes the rest pointless, and you hear about a stalled one instead of waiting on it. Your agent goes straight to the cause.
- **Link:** `/docs/guides/fix-a-red-gate`
- **Expresses:** Human benefit · [Get useful failures sooner](../feature-canon-human-benefits.md#get-useful-failures-sooner)
- **Draws on:** Normalized diagnostics (`diagnostics`) · Fail-fast cancellation (`fail-fast`) · Strand detection (`strand-detection`)

### Know what is ready

9 cards · lens: Know it's ready.

#### Finished means tested

- **Card:** `project-defined-completion` · benefit
- **Line:** Work counts as finished only when your tests, linter, and build pass.
- **Opened:** You choose the commands that define finished: your formatter, linter, build, tests, and anything else. A change isn't reported as done until they all pass.
- **Link:** `/docs/guides/finish-and-land-a-change`
- **Expresses:** Human benefit · [Know when the project's own checks have passed](../feature-canon-human-benefits.md#know-when-the-projects-own-checks-have-passed)
- **Draws on:** The quality gate (`gate`) · Declared jobs (`jobs-table`)

#### Experiment freely

- **Card:** `explicit-release-decision` · benefit
- **Line:** Rapidly iterate on new features and experiments with confidence.
- **Opened:** Each experiment runs on its own branch and merges only with your approval. Keep what passes your tests and throw the rest away.
- **Link:** `/docs/guides/finish-and-land-a-change`
- **Expresses:** Human benefit · [Keep the final say over what ships](../feature-canon-human-benefits.md#keep-the-final-say-over-what-ships)
- **Draws on:** Isolated worktrees (`worktrees`) · Landing authority is proved per invocation (`consent-attestations`) · Accept (`accept`)

#### A record that lasts

- **Card:** `evidence-that-lasts` · benefit
- **Line:** Months later, look up what a change passed before it merged.
- **Opened:** When a change merges, discern attaches its record to that commit as a Git note. The note outlives the task's folder and the agent's session, and you choose whether to share it.
- **Link:** `/docs/understand/proof`
- **Expresses:** Human benefit · [Keep the completion record with the code](../feature-canon-human-benefits.md#keep-the-completion-record-with-the-code)
- **Draws on:** Durable proof notes (`proof-notes`)

#### Main stays clean

- **Card:** `unfinished-work-stays-isolated` · benefit
- **Line:** An agent can try, fail, and retry without touching your main branch.
- **Opened:** Each task lives on its own branch in its own folder. Your main branch changes only when you approve a finished result.
- **Link:** `/docs/understand/worktrees-and-trunk`
- **Expresses:** Human benefit · [Keep unfinished work away from the shared branch](../feature-canon-human-benefits.md#keep-unfinished-work-away-from-the-shared-branch)
- **Draws on:** Isolated worktrees (`worktrees`) · Accept (`accept`)

#### Proof of what passed

- **Card:** `evidence-for-this-change` · benefit
- **Line:** Every finished change shows which of your commands passed, and on which commit.
- **Opened:** That record, a Proof, names the commit it covers. Edit the code afterward and that Proof no longer applies.
- **Link:** `/docs/understand/proof`
- **Expresses:** Human benefit · [Get proof of what passed, tied to the commit it passed on](../feature-canon-human-benefits.md#get-proof-of-what-passed-tied-to-the-commit-it-passed-on)
- **Draws on:** Proof (`proof`)

#### Tested or only claimed

- **Card:** `agent-carry-judgment-as-judgment` · benefit
- **Line:** Every result separates what passed your tests from what your agent only judged.
- **Opened:** Commands that ran show as passed or failed. An agent's answer to a review question shows apart from them, as that agent's judgment.
- **Link:** `/docs/understand/checkpoints`
- **Expresses:** Agent benefit · [Carry judgment as judgment](../feature-canon-agent-benefits.md#carry-judgment-as-judgment)
- **Draws on:** Checkpoints (`checkpoints`)

#### Pre-approve the routine

- **Card:** `bounded-standing-permission` · benefit
- **Line:** Let routine changes, like docs fixes, merge without waiting for you.
- **Opened:** Name the areas you approve in advance, such as documentation. A change that touches any file outside them still comes to you.
- **Link:** `/docs/guides/finish-and-land-a-change#pre-approve-routine-work`
- **Expresses:** Human benefit · [Pre-approve routine changes within clear boundaries](../feature-canon-human-benefits.md#pre-approve-routine-changes-within-clear-boundaries)
- **Draws on:** Landing authority is proved per invocation (`consent-attestations`) · Scopes (`scope-gates`)

#### By the time CI runs, you already know.

- **Card:** `statement-ci-confirms-what-you-know` · statement
- **Opened:** Your tests and other commands run on your machine before you share anything. CI, the checks that run after you push, then confirms a result you've already seen.
- **Link:** `/docs/guides/run-the-gate-in-ci`
- **Expresses:** Consequence · [By the time CI runs, you already know](consequence-canon.md#by-the-time-ci-runs-you-already-know)
- **Draws on:** The quality gate (`gate`)

#### Preview before it runs

- **Card:** `recover-interrupted-operations` · benefit
- **Line:** See what discern will change before it touches your project.
- **Opened:** Ask for a dry run to see the plan with nothing applied. If a command stops partway, discern keeps enough state to resume or repair it.
- **Link:** `/docs/understand/local-control`
- **Expresses:** Human benefit · [Preview changes and recover cleanly](../feature-canon-human-benefits.md#preview-changes-and-recover-cleanly)
- **Draws on:** Plan and apply (`plan-apply`) · Crash-safe provisioning (`crash-safe-provisioning`) · Clean under interruption (`interruption-safety`)

### Keep the gains the project earns

9 cards · lens: Keep quality up.

#### Gains that stick

- **Card:** `retain-measured-gains` · benefit
- **Line:** Set a limit, like minimum test coverage, that agents can't lower to pass.
- **Opened:** Every change has to meet the limit on your main branch, and loosening one takes your approval. These limits are what discern calls standards.
- **Link:** `/docs/understand/standards`
- **Expresses:** Human benefit · [Keep measurable quality gains from slipping backward](../feature-canon-human-benefits.md#keep-measurable-quality-gains-from-slipping-backward)
- **Draws on:** Standards (`standards`) · Floors and ceilings (`standards-direction`)

#### Raise the bar

- **Card:** `pin-new-baseline` · benefit
- **Line:** When test coverage improves, one command locks the gain in as the new minimum.
- **Opened:** The command tightens the limit to the new value and saves that change as its own commit. A margin you set keeps ordinary ups and downs from failing the next change.
- **Link:** `/docs/understand/standards#lock-in-a-gain`
- **Expresses:** Human benefit · [Make today's improvement tomorrow's starting point](../feature-canon-human-benefits.md#make-todays-improvement-tomorrows-starting-point)
- **Draws on:** Capturing a gain (`standards-pin`) · Limit headroom (`standards-margin`)

#### Dead links get caught

- **Card:** `catch-documentation-breakage` · benefit
- **Line:** A broken link in the docs your agents keep fails like a broken test.
- **Opened:** The same check covers section anchors and discern command examples in the project guide. Whether an explanation is still right stays a judgment for you and your agents.
- **Link:** `/docs/guides/maintain-project-map`
- **Expresses:** Human benefit · [Catch broken project documentation before it lands](../feature-canon-human-benefits.md#catch-broken-project-documentation-before-it-lands)
- **Draws on:** The docs integrity preflight (`docs-integrity`)

#### Fix it everywhere

- **Card:** `remove-bug-class` · benefit
- **Line:** Fix a bug everywhere it lives and guard against its return.
- **Opened:** A built-in playbook has your agent prove the cause, fix every instance, and add a test or lint rule that fails if the bug comes back.
- **Link:** `/docs/guides/create-and-manage-skills`
- **Expresses:** Human benefit · [Remove the cause and guard every instance of the bug class](../feature-canon-human-benefits.md#remove-the-cause-and-guard-every-instance-of-the-bug-class)
- **Draws on:** Cure a bug (`skill-cure-a-bug`)

#### Your quality bar never drops without your say-so.

- **Card:** `statement-a-project-that-only-gets-better` · statement
- **Opened:** A quality limit you set can tighten, and no change can loosen one without your approval. What the project learns is where the next session starts.
- **Link:** `/docs/understand/standards`
- **Expresses:** Consequence · [A project that only gets better](consequence-canon.md#a-project-that-only-gets-better)
- **Draws on:** Standards (`standards`) · Capturing a gain (`standards-pin`) · Agent instructions (`instructions`)

#### Clutter stays gone

- **Card:** `keep-clutter-down` · benefit
- **Line:** Clear out dead code and duplicates, and stop them piling back up.
- **Opened:** A cleanup playbook removes only what's proven safe to delete. A limit on what's left stops the count from rising again.
- **Link:** `/docs/guides/create-and-manage-skills`
- **Expresses:** Human benefit · [Keep maintenance clutter from growing back](../feature-canon-human-benefits.md#keep-maintenance-clutter-from-growing-back)
- **Draws on:** Clear the decks (`skill-clear-the-decks`) · Standards (`standards`)

#### Limits for any metric

- **Card:** `standards-that-scale` · benefit
- **Line:** Limit bundle size, lint warnings, or any number a command can print.
- **Opened:** Slow tests, duplicated code, download size: if a command can print the number, it can become a limit. A limit can be a rate, so it keeps pace as the codebase grows.
- **Link:** `/docs/understand/standards`
- **Expresses:** Human benefit · [Use standards that stay useful as the project grows](../feature-canon-human-benefits.md#use-standards-that-stay-useful-as-the-project-grows)
- **Draws on:** One-line metric protocol (`standards-metric-protocol`) · Rates, not raw counts (`standards-rates`)

#### See where agents struggle

- **Card:** `improve-practice-from-evidence` · benefit
- **Line:** Find out where your agents keep getting stuck, counted from real runs.
- **Opened:** A local activity log of what discern's commands did shows repeated failures and slow steps. It holds no code and ranks no agent.
- **Link:** `/docs/guides/improve-the-practice`
- **Expresses:** Human benefit · [Improve the way the agents work from real evidence](../feature-canon-human-benefits.md#improve-the-way-the-agents-work-from-real-evidence)
- **Draws on:** Patterns (`patterns`) · The logbook (`logbook`)

#### Migrations that finish

- **Card:** `retire-old-pattern` · benefit
- **Line:** Phase out an old library and block it from creeping back.
- **Opened:** The count of remaining uses can only fall. Once it reaches zero, a new use stops a change from passing.
- **Link:** `/docs/understand/standards`
- **Expresses:** Human benefit · [Retire an old pattern across the codebase](../feature-canon-human-benefits.md#retire-an-old-pattern-across-the-codebase)
- **Draws on:** Set the standard (`skill-set-the-standard`) · Standards (`standards`)

### Keep project knowledge available

10 cards · lens: Stop repeating yourself.

#### Teach it once

- **Card:** `teach-project-once` · benefit
- **Line:** Explain a rule once, and every agent session starts out knowing it.

- **Opened:** A short decision record captures the context, the choice, and the options you turned down. Later sessions are less likely to reopen a settled question.
- **Link:** `/docs/understand/instructions-skills-and-map`

- **Draws on:** The map (`map`)

#### One source of truth

- **Card:** `reuse-engineering-discipline` · benefit
- **Line:** A built-in playbook has agents define each value once and test every use.
- **Opened:** Each fact gets one home, and a test keeps every copy in step with it. When a list grows, its tests and docs grow with it.
- **Link:** `/docs/guides/create-and-manage-skills`
- **Expresses:** Human benefit · [Carry proven engineering practices between projects](../feature-canon-human-benefits.md#carry-proven-engineering-practices-between-projects)
- **Draws on:** Write it once (`skill-write-it-once`)

#### Your taste becomes every agent's standard.

- **Card:** `statement-taste-becomes-infrastructure` · statement
- **Opened:** Your conventions go into every agent's instructions, the numbers you care about become limits, and agents answer your review questions on matching changes. The taste stays yours: discern adds none of its own.
- **Link:** `/docs/guides/write-project-instructions`
- **Expresses:** Consequence · [Your taste becomes infrastructure](consequence-canon.md#your-taste-becomes-infrastructure)
- **Draws on:** Agent instructions (`instructions`) · Standards (`standards`) · Checkpoints (`checkpoints`)

#### Known fixes, delivered

- **Card:** `instructions-at-failure` · benefit
- **Line:** When an agent hits a problem you've seen before, it gets your written fix.
- **Opened:** Record a recurring trap once, with what to do about it. The next agent to hit it gets your note in the same result that reports the failure.
- **Link:** `/docs/guides/maintain-project-map`
- **Expresses:** Human benefit · [Put the right instructions beside the failure](../feature-canon-human-benefits.md#put-the-right-instructions-beside-the-failure)
- **Draws on:** The gotchas pointer (`gotchas-pointer`)

#### Briefings on demand

- **Card:** `export-project-briefing` · benefit
- **Line:** Export what a new teammate or agent should read as one file.
- **Opened:** Choose the project guide's public pages, a named reading list, or a hand-picked set. The reader gets them in a set order instead of a documentation dump.
- **Link:** `/docs/guides/maintain-project-map`
- **Expresses:** Human benefit · [Export the right project briefing for the next reader](../feature-canon-human-benefits.md#export-the-right-project-briefing-for-the-next-reader)
- **Draws on:** The map browser (`map-browser`)

### Put a serious practice in place

9 cards · lens: Safe to try.

#### Agent-led setup

- **Card:** `agent-commissioning` · benefit
- **Line:** Your coding agent installs and fine-tunes discern for your project.
- **Opened:** It studies your repository, connects the commands you already use, and asks you a short batch of questions. Setup usually takes 20 to 40 minutes and counts as done only when your tests pass in a fresh copy of the project.
- **Link:** `/docs/start/installation-and-setup`
- **Expresses:** Human benefit · [Have your agent set up the practice for this project](../feature-canon-human-benefits.md#have-your-agent-set-up-the-practice-for-this-project)
- **Draws on:** Agent-driven setup (`setup`)

#### Tidy up safely

- **Card:** `clean-abandoned-environments` · benefit
- **Line:** Delete old tasks, and recover their committed work if you change your mind.
- **Opened:** Removing a task frees its folder, ports, and databases. Each recently removed task keeps its last commit, so committed work can come back.
- **Link:** `/docs/guides/recover-an-interrupted-task#recover-a-dropped-branch`
- **Expresses:** Human benefit · [Clean up abandoned tasks without a cliff edge](../feature-canon-human-benefits.md#clean-up-abandoned-tasks-without-a-cliff-edge)
- **Draws on:** Bounded drop recovery (`drop-recovery`) · Owned worktree reclamation (`worktree-prune`)

#### 1 Config file

- **Card:** `numeral-one-config-file` · numeral
- **Line:** Every discern setting for your project lives in a single readable file.
- **Opened:** Your instructions, project guide, and agent files sit beside it as ordinary files you own.
- **Link:** `/docs/reference/config-reference`
- **Expresses:** Claim · [`one-config-file`](claims-and-evidence.md#one-config-file--one-configuration-file-governs-the-installation)
- **Draws on:** A one-file footprint (`one-file-footprint`)

#### Try it on the project that matters.

- **Card:** `statement-try-it-where-it-matters` · statement
- **Opened:** Setup usually takes your agent 20 to 40 minutes. Leaving takes one command and keeps every file you wrote.
- **Link:** `/docs/start/installation-and-setup`
- **Expresses:** Consequence · [Try it on the project that matters](consequence-canon.md#try-it-on-the-project-that-matters)
- **Draws on:** Agent-driven setup (`setup`) · Uninstall (`uninstall`) · File ownership (`ownership-buckets`)

#### Built with itself

- **Card:** `inspect-live-example` · benefit
- **Line:** Every change to discern is made with discern itself.
- **Opened:** Its own development uses separate tasks, quality limits, and a record of what passed for every merged change. That's the same setup it brings to your project.
- **Expresses:** Human benefit · [Inspect discern working under its own practice](../feature-canon-human-benefits.md#inspect-discern-working-under-its-own-practice)
- **Draws on:** Run on itself (`dogfooding`)

#### A built-in health check

- **Card:** `agent-manage-the-installation-lifecycle` · benefit
- **Line:** If discern stops working, one command finds the problem and names the fix.
- **Opened:** Ask your agent to check the installation. It runs the check, applies the fixes it can, and tells you what it needs from you.
- **Link:** `/docs/guides/maintain-or-remove-discern`
- **Expresses:** Agent benefit · [Manage the installation lifecycle](../feature-canon-agent-benefits.md#manage-the-installation-lifecycle)
- **Draws on:** Doctor (`doctor`)

#### Nothing to host

- **Card:** `small-installation-footprint` · benefit
- **Line:** Add discern with no account, server, or service to set up.
- **Opened:** It's one program that runs on your own machine. Your project needs Git and nothing else new.
- **Link:** `/docs/understand/local-control`
- **Expresses:** Human benefit · [Adopt discern without running another service](../feature-canon-human-benefits.md#adopt-discern-without-running-another-service)
- **Draws on:** One self-contained binary (`single-binary`) · Install and lifecycle (`install`)

#### 40 Limits it must meet

- **Card:** `numeral-limits-on-itself` · numeral
- **Line:** Every change to discern has to pass them, from test coverage to reading level.
- **Opened:** Others cap its download size, its duplicated code, and its lint exceptions. You can set the same kind of limit on your own project.
- **Expresses:** Claim · [`runs-on-itself`](claims-and-evidence.md#runs-on-itself--discern-runs-on-itself)
- **Draws on:** Run on itself (`dogfooding`)

#### Add it the week your project gets real users.

- **Card:** `statement-get-serious-when-it-gets-real` · statement
- **Opened:** A first paying user or a first collaborator can arrive without warning. Setup usually takes your agent 20 to 40 minutes.
- **Link:** `/docs/start`
- **Expresses:** Consequence · [Get serious the week it gets real](consequence-canon.md#get-serious-the-week-it-gets-real)
- **Draws on:** Agent-driven setup (`setup`)

### Change tools without starting over

9 cards · lens: Fits your tools.

#### Switch agents freely

- **Card:** `switch-providers` · benefit
- **Line:** Change coding agents without explaining your project all over again.
- **Opened:** Your instructions, quality limits, and project guide belong to the project. Connect another supported agent and discern writes the files it reads from the same sources.
- **Link:** `/docs/guides/connect-a-coding-agent`
- **Expresses:** Human benefit · [Switch coding agents without re-teaching the project](../feature-canon-human-benefits.md#switch-coding-agents-without-re-teaching-the-project)
- **Draws on:** Agent providers (`providers`) · Author once, compile everywhere (`instructions-compile`)

#### Leave without losing work

- **Card:** `retain-work-after-uninstall` · benefit
- **Line:** Uninstall with one command and keep everything you and your agents wrote.
- **Opened:** Your instructions, project guide, playbooks, and settings stay as ordinary files in your repository. Only discern's wiring goes.
- **Link:** `/docs/guides/maintain-or-remove-discern`
- **Expresses:** Human benefit · [Uninstall cleanly and keep everything you wrote](../feature-canon-human-benefits.md#uninstall-cleanly-and-keep-everything-you-wrote)
- **Draws on:** Uninstall (`uninstall`) · File ownership (`ownership-buckets`)

#### What you teach your agents stays in your repository.

- **Card:** `statement-what-agents-learn-you-own` · statement
- **Opened:** Instructions, playbooks, the project guide, and decision records are ordinary files in your repository. Back them up, hand them over, or take them elsewhere.
- **Link:** `/docs/reference/files-and-ownership`
- **Expresses:** Consequence · [Everything your agents learn becomes something you own](consequence-canon.md#everything-your-agents-learn-becomes-something-you-own)
- **Draws on:** File ownership (`ownership-buckets`) · Agent instructions (`instructions`) · Skills (`skills`) · The map (`map`)

#### Any language, any stack

- **Card:** `practice-across-stacks` · benefit
- **Line:** Work the same way in every project, whatever it's written in.
- **Opened:** Your project's own commands do the checking, so any language or framework works. It needs Git, and it runs on macOS, Linux, and Windows through WSL 2.
- **Link:** `/docs/start/how-discern-works`
- **Expresses:** Human benefit · [Use the same working practice across different stacks](../feature-canon-human-benefits.md#use-the-same-working-practice-across-different-stacks)
- **Draws on:** Stack-neutral (`stack-neutral`)

#### 5 Coding agents supported

- **Card:** `numeral-supported-coding-agents` · numeral
- **Line:** Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Cursor, and GitHub Copilot all read the same instructions.
- **Opened:** Gemini and GitHub Copilot here mean their command-line tools. Use one agent or several, and each reads the same project instructions in the file it expects.
- **Link:** `/docs/reference/platforms-and-providers`
- **Expresses:** Claim · [`one-instruction-source`](claims-and-evidence.md#one-instruction-source--every-configured-provider-receives-the-same-project-instructions)

#### Upgrade on your schedule

- **Card:** `planned-upgrades` · benefit
- **Line:** See what an upgrade will change, then update when it suits you.
- **Opened:** The program never updates itself. Release notes show what's new, and teammates on an older version hear when to catch up.
- **Link:** `/docs/guides/maintain-or-remove-discern`
- **Expresses:** Human benefit · [Choose when to upgrade](../feature-canon-human-benefits.md#choose-when-to-upgrade)
- **Draws on:** Upgrade and migrations (`upgrade`) · Release information when requested (`release-awareness`)

#### Every agent faces the same rules and tests.

- **Card:** `statement-the-same-interview-for-every-agent` · statement
- **Opened:** A new coding agent reads the same instructions and has to pass the same commands as the last one. Its work comes back with the same kind of record of what passed.
- **Link:** `/docs/guides/connect-a-coding-agent`
- **Expresses:** Consequence · [Every new agent walks into the same interview](consequence-canon.md#every-new-agent-walks-into-the-same-interview)
- **Draws on:** Agent providers (`providers`) · Author once, compile everywhere (`instructions-compile`)

#### One task, two agents

- **Card:** `agent-switch-supported-agent-hosts` · benefit
- **Line:** Start a task with one coding agent and finish it with another.
- **Opened:** A task's branch, setup, and results live in the project instead of in one tool's chat history. Any supported agent you've connected can ask where things stand and carry on.
- **Link:** `/docs/guides/connect-a-coding-agent`
- **Expresses:** Agent benefit · [Switch supported agent hosts](../feature-canon-agent-benefits.md#switch-supported-agent-hosts)
- **Draws on:** Agent providers (`providers`)

#### Scriptable by design

- **Card:** `build-on-published-contracts` · benefit
- **Line:** Get any result as JSON with a published schema for your scripts.
- **Opened:** The terminal, your agent, and your own tools all read the same result. Nothing has to scrape text meant for people.
- **Link:** `/docs/reference/mcp-and-results`
- **Expresses:** Human benefit · [Build integrations against published contracts](../feature-canon-human-benefits.md#build-integrations-against-published-contracts)

### Keep control of the project

4 cards · lens: Safe to try.

#### No API key

- **Card:** `local-without-another-model` · benefit
- **Line:** No AI model inside, so there's no API key and no extra model bill.
- **Opened:** It runs your project's own commands and records the results. Your coding agent still uses its own model provider.
- **Link:** `/docs/understand/local-control`
- **Expresses:** Human benefit · [Run discern locally without another model or API key](../feature-canon-human-benefits.md#run-discern-locally-without-another-model-or-api-key)
- **Draws on:** No model inside (`no-model-inside`)

#### Stays in its lane

- **Card:** `explicit-write-authority` · benefit
- **Line:** Every place discern can write is on a list you can read.
- **Opened:** Before you approve setup, you see what it will add. A command that writes to Git checks first that it can, so it stops before it starts instead of failing halfway.
- **Link:** `/docs/reference/files-and-ownership`
- **Expresses:** Human benefit · [Make write authority explicit](../feature-canon-human-benefits.md#make-write-authority-explicit)
- **Draws on:** Placement is consent (`placement-consent`) · Git write authority proven first (`write-preflight`)

#### Work keeps moving until it needs your yes.

- **Card:** `statement-decisions-wait-for-the-person` · statement
- **Opened:** Agents keep working, and wait on each other where they need to. A change that needs your approval waits, tested and ready, until you give it.
- **Link:** `/docs/guides/finish-and-land-a-change`
- **Expresses:** Consequence · [The decisions that need you wait for you. Everything else keeps moving.](consequence-canon.md#the-decisions-that-need-you-wait-for-you-everything-else-keeps-moving)
- **Draws on:** Awaiting a fleet condition (`await`) · Landing authority is proved per invocation (`consent-attestations`) · Accept (`accept`)

#### No telemetry

- **Card:** `agent-diagnose-workflow-friction-locally` · benefit
- **Line:** What discern records stays on your machine, and it sends no telemetry.
- **Opened:** Its activity log holds names, timings, and results, with no code or command output, and you can switch it off. Checking for updates opens the release page in your browser with your version number, and nothing else leaves your machine through discern.
- **Link:** `/docs/reference/logbook`
- **Expresses:** Agent benefit · [Diagnose workflow friction locally](../feature-canon-agent-benefits.md#diagnose-workflow-friction-locally)
- **Draws on:** Evidence stays local (`local-evidence`) · The logbook (`logbook`)

## Benefits without a card

- None: every human benefit has a card.

## Coverage and traceability

Every card cites a live entry of its source's registry and draws on at least one live feature node that the entry rests on. Every human benefit has a card or a recorded reason for its absence, and the wall's clusters are the Human Benefit Canon's clusters. The guard (`tests/site_wall_deck_test.ts`) holds all of it, together with the copy limits, the links, and the counts a numeral card states.
